answer: A useful defense is to require each agent to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it can influence shared decisions. When agents make inconsistent claims or collude to approve a fraudulent transaction, a challenge process can expose the conflict and destroy some of that stake. This makes a hollow identity costly: creating a tide of fake agents requires funding each one, while risking that a single proven attack forfeits the pearl of capital it was meant to protect. The defense raises the attacker’s cost; it does not prove that one stake represents one real person.
